design_summary.purpose: Parameterized 8-bit PWM controller that maintains a synchronous counter, wraps the count to zero at the programmed period, and drives a PWM output based on a compare against the duty cycle.
design_summary.operating_model: Single-clock-domain design in which all sequential state updates on the rising edge of clk. reset_n is active-low and synchronously clears state to zero. When enable is high, the counter increments unless it has reached period, in which case it wraps to zero on the next enabled clock edge. When enable is low, the counter holds. pwm_out is a combinational function of the current registered counter_value and duty_cycle.

external_interfaces.name: clk
external_interfaces.description: Primary clock for all sequential state.

external_interfaces.name: reset_n
external_interfaces.description: Synchronous active-low reset that clears sequential state.

external_interfaces.name: enable
external_interfaces.description: Counter update control; when low the counter holds its current value.

external_interfaces.name: duty_cycle
external_interfaces.description: Programmable compare threshold used to generate pwm_out.

external_interfaces.name: period
external_interfaces.description: Programmable wrap threshold for the counter.

external_interfaces.name: pwm_out
external_interfaces.description: PWM waveform output asserted when counter_value is less than duty_cycle.

module_architecture.name: pwm_controller
module_architecture.role: Top-level and only described module; owns the PWM counter state and output generation.
responsibilities: Honor synchronous active-low reset by clearing all registers to zero.
Generate pwm_out as a pure comparison of counter_value and duty_cycle.
Wrap the counter to zero on the cycle after it reaches period while enabled.
Expose counter_value as a direct observable output of the internal counter state.
interface_notes: Receives clk, reset_n, enable, duty_cycle, and period as the complete input set.
Drives pwm_out and counter_value as the complete output set.
duty_cycle and period are sampled synchronously and used combinationally in the same clock domain.
No internal clock gating is described; behavior remains fully synchronous to clk.
ownership_notes: Owns the sequential counter state that backs counter_value.
Owns the combinational compare that determines pwm_out.
Owns synchronous reset behavior for all state elements.
Owns wrap decision logic based on the current counter_value and period.

data_flow_summary: clk and reset_n control all sequential updates in the single clock domain.
enable gates counter advancement; when deasserted, counter_value holds its prior registered value.
period is compared against the current counter_value to determine whether the next enabled increment wraps to zero.
duty_cycle is compared against the current counter_value to generate pwm_out combinationally.
counter_value is both the registered state observation and the source operand for the PWM compare and wrap decision.

clock_reset_summary.clocking: All logic is synchronous to clk in a single 50.0 MHz domain with a 20.0 ns period.
clock_reset_summary.reset_behavior: reset_n is active-low and synchronous; when low, all sequential state is cleared to 8'h00 on the next rising clock edge. After reset is applied, counter_value reads as zero and pwm_out evaluates low when duty_cycle is zero, consistent with the compare against the cleared counter.

integration_notes: The design is self-contained and has no internal submodules, memory macros, or additional clock domains.
The external contract expects counter_value to be a registered output and pwm_out to reflect the current compare without extra sequencing.
The described behavior matches the specified feature contracts for reset, enabled increment, disabled hold, and wrap-at-period operation.
